newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian cement plant back to work after tragedy.
newsitem.headline: Colombian cement plant back to work after tragedy.

text.p: Cement production has resumed at Cementos Diamante's Caracolito plant in central Colombia, where 10 people were killed in a fiery accident last Friday, a company spokeswoman said.
She said work at the plant had resumed Sunday and that production -- estimated at 1.3 million metric tons per year -- was now back to normal.

Friday's accident at the ultra-modern plant in the city of Ibague was caused by a blockage in one of the pre-heaters that a mix of raw materials pass through before being blended at extremely high temperatures into cement, company sources said.
Local hospital officials in Ibague said 10 people were killed when a cloud of red-hot material exploded through a conduit and rained down on plant workers in a virtual avalanche.

The Diamante spokeswoman said there was no significant damage to the plant despite the seriousness of the accident, which analysts at Flemings Research in New York described as "one of the most unusual (and truly appalling) incidents" in the recent history of cement manufacturing.
